findings.finding: Simple-mode's launch_coder -> run_coder path never commits agent-written files to git before get_diff() is called. This is the exact bug Day 14 fixed for the full-mode run_manager() path (git_add+git_commit added there), but the fix was never applied to launch_coder, and coder.py/tools.py's submit_patch tool only records files_changed locally without ever running git add/git commit.
findings.evidence: grep for git_add/git_commit in coder.py returns no matches; tools.py:970-973 submit_patch just sets patch_result dict fields; agents.py launch_coder (604-722) has no git commit step before get_diff() at line 694; tests/test_launch_coder_bootstrap.py:170 mocks app.api.agents.get_diff to return "" directly, masking this from test coverage.
findings.production_impact: Every simple-mode task's diff shown for human review is empty even though files were actually written to the worktree filesystem -- the human approves blind, and files_changed is reported as non-empty while diff is empty, an internally inconsistent, misleading task record.
findings.recommendation: Add the same git_add()+git_commit() step manager.py:263-287 uses, either inside run_coder() itself or in launch_coder() right after run_coder() returns files_changed, before calling get_diff().
findings.fix_note: Added git_add()+git_commit() to launch_coder() (agents.py), mirroring manager.py's existing pattern exactly. Test: TestOrch04_001_LaunchCoderCommits in test_audit04_orchestration_fixes.py. NOT executed (no Python interpreter available).

findings.finding: "completed" is defined as a status value but is never the target of any transition anywhere in the codebase (11 transition_task call sites checked, none target "completed", and can_transition() rejects it from every state since it's absent from every state's transition list). The real terminal-ish status, "ready_for_review", is reused to mean two different things across a task's lifecycle (plan awaiting approval vs. code diff awaiting merge), and POST /{task_id}/approve's only guard is status=="ready_for_review", with no way to distinguish which meaning applies.
findings.evidence: db/models.py:47 ("completed": []); grep -rn "transition_task(" backend/app -- 11 hits, none pass "completed"; tasks.py:280-284 approve_task's sole status guard.
findings.production_impact: No task in either pipeline mode ever reaches a real terminal done state -- tasks sit at ready_for_review forever, even after a PR is pushed (dispatch_git_push_decision only updates pr_url/pr_status, never DevTask.status). Re-clicking approve on a code-complete simple-mode task passes the same guard used for plan-approval and silently re-launches launch_coder from scratch, re-running the coder a second time with no warning.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a real terminal status (e.g. reaching "completed" when pr_status becomes "pushed" or on explicit human close-out), and make approve_task branch on pipeline_state.stage or presence of task.diff rather than trusting the overloaded status string alone.
findings.fix_note: Added "completed" to ready_for_review's VALID_TRANSITIONS. approve_task now 409s when task.diff is not None. Added POST /api/tasks/{id}/complete. dispatch_git_push_decision() auto-completes on a successful push. Tests: TestOrch04_002_TerminalState. NOT executed.

findings.finding: All three concurrency semaphores are fully implemented and unit-tested in isolation (tests/test_concurrency.py) but have zero real callers anywhere in the dispatch path -- neither launch_manager/run_manager nor run_epic_manager acquires any of them before dispatching work.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "epic_slot(|agent_run_slot(|subtask_slot(" backend/app outside concurrency.py and tests/ returns zero results; manager.py's run_manager()/run_epic_manager() read in full, no async with epic_slot()/agent_run_slot()/subtask_slot(...) anywhere.
findings.production_impact: max_concurrent_epics/max_concurrent_agent_runs/max_concurrent_subtasks_per_epic are dead configuration -- a burst of concurrent task launches has no backpressure mechanism actually engaged despite one being fully built and configured. subtask_slot's real-world impact is smaller than it looks since run_manager()'s own subtask loop is already sequential (not gathered/parallelized); epic_slot/agent_run_slot are the two with genuine cross-task concurrency exposure.
findings.recommendation: Wrap launch_manager's dispatch into run_manager (per-agent-run granularity) and run_epic_manager's top level with the corresponding async with slot acquisition.
findings.fix_note: agent_run_slot() wrapped around each of the 3 real per-subtask agent dispatches; subtask_slot() around each subtask's retry loop (manual __aenter__/__aexit__ to avoid re-indenting the loop, safe since nothing in it raises past this function). run_epic_manager() split into a thin epic_slot()-holding wrapper + _run_epic_manager_body(). Tests: TestOrch04_009_ConcurrencySlots. NOT executed.

findings.finding: check_file_conflicts()'s own module docstring claims it is "Called before dispatching a coder/backend-dev/frontend-dev subtask" -- false as of this audit. Zero real callers and zero test coverage found anywhere.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "check_file_conflicts(" backend/app outside its own definition returns zero results; grep -rn "check_file_conflicts" backend/tests also returns zero; manager.py read in full with no import of conflict_guard.
findings.production_impact: Two concurrent epics/tasks whose plans both touch an overlapping file can have their dev agents write to the same file in two different worktrees with zero detection or blocking -- the exact scenario this module exists to prevent, per its own docstring, silently does not happen.
findings.recommendation: Call check_file_conflicts(candidate_files, current_epic_id, db) in run_epic_manager() before run_manager() is invoked, using impacted_files from the architect plan; surface a conflict as blocked/human-review rather than proceeding.
findings.fix_note: check_file_conflicts() wired into _run_epic_manager_body() before coding starts; halts the epic with a real conflict description on overlap. SECOND BUG FOUND AND FIXED while wiring this in: conflict_guard._get_epic_files() only accepted bare-string impacted_files entries, but architect.py's real submit_architect_plan schema always produces {"path":..., "reason":...} objects -- the function would have returned an empty locked-files set for every real epic, silently defeating the whole guard even after wiring. Fixed to accept both shapes. Tests: TestOrch04_010_ConflictGuard. NOT executed.

findings.finding: Subtask.status defaults to "pending" at creation and is never updated anywhere afterward -- no UPDATE statement anywhere touches this column. run_manager()'s real per-subtask outcome is only ever kept in an in-memory results list, never persisted back onto the Subtask row.
findings.evidence: models.py:192 (default="pending"); grep -rn "Subtask).where|update(Subtask)|\.status = " backend/app finds no UPDATE on Subtask, only the SELECT in list_subtasks.
findings.production_impact: GET /api/tasks/{id}/subtasks always reports every subtask as "pending" regardless of its real completed/blocked outcome -- a real, user-visible inaccuracy in the per-subtask progress dashboard.
findings.recommendation: Add update_subtask_status(db, subtask_id, status) and call it from run_manager()'s or launch_manager()'s per-subtask result handling.
findings.fix_note: Added update_subtask_status() to repository.py. run_manager() fetches the task's real Subtask rows once (position-correlated with the subtasks list, since the decomposer's transient "id" field is never persisted as the real DB primary key) and persists each subtask's final status. Test: TestOrch04_011_SubtaskStatusPersistence. NOT executed.

findings.finding: remove_worktree() is fully implemented but has zero real callers anywhere, including tests -- nothing ever reclaims a worktree on any code path. create_worktree()'s existence check silently reuses a pre-existing directory with no validation it's a clean, correctly-registered worktree on the expected branch.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "remove_worktree" backend matches only its own definition; worktree.py:38-39 unconditional early return with no git worktree list/branch verification.
findings.production_impact: Worktree directories accumulate forever (unbounded disk growth). Combined with /restart having no in-progress guard (ORCH-04-004) and reusing the same task_id/worktree path, a restarted task silently builds on top of a stale/dirty worktree left over from a prior failed attempt instead of a clean checkout, with no signal this happened.
findings.recommendation: Wire remove_worktree() into task completion/rejection or a scheduled cleanup sweep matching the existing retention.py pattern; validate an existing wt_path (git worktree list membership + branch match) before reusing it.
findings.fix_note: create_worktree() now validates a pre-existing directory via `git worktree list --porcelain` before trusting it (new _is_registered_worktree() helper); rebuilds cleanly (removing the stale worktree + branch first) if not registered. remove_worktree() wired into reject_task, complete_task, and the successful-push path in dispatch_git_push_decision(). Tests: TestOrch04_012_WorktreeCleanup. NOT executed.

findings.finding: restart_task force-sets DevTask.status="pending" via a raw UPDATE, bypassing can_transition() entirely, with no check for whether a background dispatch (launch_manager/launch_coder) is already actively running for that task_id.
findings.evidence: tasks.py:232-236 raw update(DevTask) bypassing transition_task/can_transition; no lock/mutex/in-progress check anywhere in launch_manager/launch_coder/restart_task.
findings.production_impact: Calling /restart while a manager run is still in-flight produces two concurrent orchestration runs against the same task_id and the same worktree (create_worktree silently hands back the same directory), with interleaved git operations and duplicated agent-run cost.
findings.recommendation: Add an in-progress guard (e.g. checking for an active AgentRun with status="running" for the task) that /restart and other launch triggers check before dispatching.
findings.fix_note: /restart now 409s if task.status is planning/coding/testing (the only statuses set at the start of an in-flight background pipeline run and held until it finishes). Test: TestOrch04_004_RestartGuard. NOT executed.

findings.finding: The 409 "already decided" check reads PendingApproval.status synchronously, but the actual status flip only happens inside a FastAPI background task (arecord_decision, called via resume_planning_pipeline/dispatch_git_push_decision) that runs AFTER the HTTP response is returned -- a TOCTOU window where the row is still "pending" when it should already be considered decided.
findings.evidence: approvals.py:114-130 read-check-then-background-dispatch with no synchronous state flip; approval_gate.py:157-192 _record_decision is the only status-flipping code, reached only via the background-scheduled _dispatch_decision.
findings.production_impact: A second approve/reject call for the same thread, arriving in the window before the first background task executes, sees a stale "pending" status, passes the 409 check, and dispatches a second concurrent resume_planning_pipeline()/dispatch_git_push_decision() call -- double-approval or double-push-processing.
findings.recommendation: Flip PendingApproval.status synchronously inside the endpoint before scheduling the background task, so the 409 check reflects reality at read time.
findings.fix_note: Extracted _decide_or_409(): flips PendingApproval.status synchronously via arecord_decision() inside the endpoint, before scheduling the background dispatch; the DB update's own result is the source of truth for the 409 check. Also fixed a second gap found in the process: the git_push action path never called arecord_decision() at all before this change. Tests: TestOrch04_007_ApprovalRace. NOT executed.

findings.finding: asyncio.create_task(...) is used at 3 real call sites with the returned Task object immediately discarded (no retained reference) -- the specific hazard Python's own asyncio.create_task documentation warns about (a task may be garbage-collected mid-execution if nothing holds a strong reference).
findings.evidence: agents.py:291 (launch_manager dispatch, discarded), agents.py:423-427 and 543/547 (logging/heartbeat closures, discarded). Contrast with background_tasks.add_task(...) used everywhere else in the same file, which IS tracked.
findings.production_impact: The launch_manager dispatch after plan approval -- the step that starts real coding work -- has no tracked reference and no FastAPI-level completion guarantee, unlike every other dispatch in the codebase. Rarely manifests in current CPython but is not a guaranteed-safe pattern.
findings.recommendation: Route launch_manager's dispatch through BackgroundTasks (pass it through from the calling endpoint) or retain the task reference in a module-level set with a done-callback, per the standard asyncio idiom.
findings.fix_note: Added _spawn_tracked() (module-level set + done-callback, the standard asyncio idiom) in agents.py; all 4 real asyncio.create_task() call sites (launch_manager dispatch, on_status/heartbeat/on_tool closures in launch_manager/launch_planner/launch_coder) now use it. Test: TestOrch04_014_SpawnTracked. NOT executed.

findings.location: run_manager retry loop, run_backend_dev/run_frontend_dev retry loop
findings.finding: run_manager()'s per-subtask retry loop and run_backend_dev()/run_frontend_dev()'s internal static-check retry loop both key off the same settings.max_retries (default 3), multiplying to up to 9 real attempts for one subtask with no backoff between any of them. manager_max_subtask_retries is defined specifically for the outer loop's purpose but is never referenced anywhere.
findings.evidence: manager.py:115 max_retries = settings.max_retries; backend_dev.py:122,125 same setting reused one level deeper; grep -rn "manager_max_subtask_retries" backend/app finds only its own definition.
findings.production_impact: During a sustained Anthropic outage/rate-limit window, retry amplification wastes up to 3x more real API calls per subtask than the configured budget implies, with no cooldown -- added load exactly when the upstream is already struggling. Task still reaches a clean blocked status eventually (see Phase 6C scenario 1) -- cost/efficiency issue, not a correctness one.
findings.recommendation: Use manager_max_subtask_retries for the outer loop instead of reusing max_retries; add exponential backoff between attempts in at least the outer loop.
findings.fix_note: run_manager()'s outer loop now uses manager_max_subtask_retries instead of the shared max_retries. Added exponential backoff (asyncio.sleep(0.5 * 2**attempt)) before each retry. Tests: TestOrch04_008_015_RetryWiring. NOT executed.

findings.evidence: grep for failure_ladder.rollback(/resume(/should_retry( outside tests/ returns no call sites.
findings.production_impact: Low -- the ladder still functions via its other 4 wired rungs (checkpoint/escalate/abort/request_human_review), but the module's own docstring presents all 6 as equally real.
findings.recommendation: Wire should_retry() into the existing range(max_retries) loops (also fixes ORCH-04-015), or document rollback/resume/should_retry as intentionally manual/operator tooling.
findings.fix_note: should_retry() wired into run_manager()'s, run_backend_dev()'s, and run_frontend_dev()'s retry-bound checks (same semantics as the prior manual attempt==max_retries-1 comparisons, now via the ladder's own function). rollback()/resume() explicitly documented as intentionally manual/operator-invoked tooling (not auto-wired -- a judgment call, matching the prompt_registry.deploy() precedent) rather than force-wired. NOT executed (should_retry wiring covered by TestOrch04_008_015_RetryWiring).

findings.finding: The entire queue-abstraction module has zero real callers -- all real task dispatch in tasks.py goes directly through FastAPI BackgroundTasks, bypassing this abstraction (and the RQ/Redis backend it supports) entirely.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "queue_adapter\.|from app.pipeline.queue_adapter import" backend/app outside the module and tests/ returns zero results; every dispatch call site in tasks.py uses background_tasks.add_task directly.
findings.production_impact: QUEUE_BACKEND=rq has zero effect on real task dispatch today despite being an actively-validated config option, which is surprising given the setting's existence.
findings.recommendation: Wire real dispatch call sites through queue().enqueue(...) instead of raw BackgroundTasks, or explicitly document this as not-yet-integrated infrastructure.
findings.fix_note: Documented rather than wired -- added an explicit module-level note to queue_adapter.py explaining real dispatch bypasses it and why this wasn't force-wired during this pass (BackgroundTasks vs. a real queue worker are different failure models -- a deliberate architectural decision needing its own scoped review, not a drive-by fix alongside unrelated orchestration changes, per the audit's own Large effort estimate). Test: TestOrch04_016_QueueAdapterDocumented (sanity-checks the documented state, doesn't test new behavior).

app/agents/tools.py and app/agents/chat_agent.py each unconditionally imported the POSIX-only `fcntl` module, causing 176 test-collection errors suite-wide. Fixed the same way (sys.platform guard + daemon-thread-based non-blocking read on Windows).
